title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face, starting with the first loop. In this loop, draw the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0), then draw the second line from (0.75, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.125). Continue by drawing the third line from (0.75, 0.125) to (0.0, 0.125), and finally, draw the fourth line from (0.0, 0.125) back to the origin. Apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire two-dimensional sketch to reduce its size proportionally. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it with the same translation vector. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch 0.0469 units along the normal direction to create the three-dimensional model. Ensure that the extrusion does not extend in the opposite direction. Finally, integrate the part by creating a new solid body from the extrusion. The dimensions of the final part are 0.7500000000000001 units in length, 0.12500000000000003 units in width, and 0.04687500000000001 units in height.

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.125, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.125, 0.0469) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0469) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

import cadquery as cq

# Part 1: Rectangular Object
part_1 = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0.125).lineTo(0, 0.125).close() \
    .extrude(0.0469)

# Part 2: Circular Cutouts
part_2 = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0.0063, 0.0063).circle(0.0063) \
    .moveTo(0.125, 0.0063).circle(0.0063) \
    .moveTo(0.2437, 0.0063).circle(0.0063) \
    .extrude(-0.125, combine=False)

# Combine part_1 and part_2
r = part_1.cut(part_2)
